intention: Teach cairn/devices/inference_domain/host.py:_post to refuse a host response that carries no answer, with a name distinct from HostUnmetered. The measured shape: HTTP 200, no `error` key, 96 bytes — {"model":"","created_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"","content":""},"done":false} — Go's zero-valued api.ChatResponse, returned when ollama collected nothing from the runner and reported it as success. _post's existing gate checks `status >= 400 or body.get('error')` and is blind to it by construction, so the body travels on and the refusal finally happens two layers later at metered_cost, which says 'the host reported no token counters'. That sentence is true and points at the wrong thing: an answer we cannot price and an answer that does not exist are different events with different owners.
why: A diagnostic surface that names the wrong failure costs the next mind the whole diagnosis. THE LIVED SYMPTOM, measured: this was chased across FOUR drives of aider-builds-a-piece as an intermittent host flake, with num_ctx, ask size and the resolve cache each raised as hypotheses and each killed in turn, because the only thing any surface ever said was 'no token counters'. It was cornered in the end by capturing the exact /api/chat payload and replaying it with curl — 3/3 identical 96-byte failures in 0.1s while the host was wedged, and 3/3 clean passes with prompt_eval_count 9,359 and done_reason 'stop' on the identical bytes twenty minutes later. Every one of those hours was spent re-deriving what the raw body says in its first field (Law 1). This is also the SECOND instance of a shape host.py already named in its own filed edge — /api/embeddings 'returns only the vector', met by refusing the endpoint rather than metering zero, with HostUnmetered's docstring calling the failure 'shape intact while draining its meaning'. Two instances with different fixes (one ours to route around, one the host's to fix and ours to report) want two names.
traces_to: Law 7 — errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces and permanent in records of truth; a surface that collapses 'no answer' into 'no price' has collapsed the error. Law 3 — the wedge was unmeasurable-by-narration until an instrument read the raw body; the refusal makes the next occurrence self-reporting at n=1. Law 10 — 'we have not built the measurement yet' was the true state here, and this builds it.
gates: prove_gate: the tester runs cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/ under isolation and seals a VALIDATION beside the code — verdict and seal from the same hand. The proof grips at the transport seam, which host.py already makes injectable ('Injectable so the proofs never need a live host'), so no live host is needed and the captured 96 bytes ride as a fixture. extra_gates: durability — committed and pushed, on the emit chokepoint. kicks_back_on: a red proof routes back to build at the point of creation (CP2). Bound additionally by this node's own shape: the new refusal must be exercised by a mutation that removes it, since a check whose absence changes no test is not a check.
falsifier: DONE when a proof drives host._post with a transport returning HTTP 200 and the captured 96-byte zero-value body, and _post raises a refusal that (a) is distinct from HostUnmetered, (b) carries the body verbatim, and (c) says the host returned no answer rather than no counters — while the same _post still returns normally for a body carrying counters, and still raises HostRefused for a 4xx and for an `error` key. The refusal is measured against the REAL captured bytes, kept as a fixture, not a hand-typed approximation. WRONG-INTENT if the check also fires on a legitimate response: a legitimately empty completion (a model that stops immediately) WITH counters must still pass, which is why the test cannot be 'content is empty' alone. If that case turns out to be indistinguishable from the wedge, the split is in the wrong place and this ticket killed itself rather than failing.
horizon: one build for the falsifier; the watch's horizon is 10 recorded refusals across the two arms, or the first misfiling, whichever comes first.
children: none, because the seam is one function (host.py:_post, ~14 lines) plus its proof, and the one thing that could have been a child — the host-side cause of the wedge — is explicitly out of scope and is not a code-seam at all (nothing on this box is edited to fix it).
dependencies: none. host.py's transport is already injectable and the fixture bytes are captured.
distinctions_recorded: DETECTION IS NOT THE DEFECT — THE NAME IS. metered_cost already refuses correctly and must keep refusing; its job is pricing and it is right to decline to price an answerless response. What it cannot do is say WHY, because by the time it sees the payload the HTTP status and the raw body are gone. The refusal belongs where both are in scope, which is _post and nowhere else.

THE THREE TELLS, so the check is not 'content is empty': `done` is FALSE (a finished non-streaming response is always true), `done_reason` is ABSENT, and the counters are absent — on top of an empty message and a zero-valued `model` and `created_at`. A legitimately empty completion has done true, a done_reason, and counters. Building the check on the empty content alone is the coin-toss-red version of this ticket.

WHAT WEDGES AND WHAT CLEARS THE HOST IS UNMEASURED, n=1 on the transition. Observed: while wedged, every request returns the zero value instantly, including a one-message request; after a streaming request and some minutes, everything passed including the full payload. Whether the stream request cleared it, whether time did, or whether something else did, is not known — and the hex-side ollama log was never read. Deliberately out of scope: the seam-side refusal is buildable and provable without it, and bundling an unbounded host investigation into a code-seam is how a ticket stops being finishable. Recorded so it is a known unknown rather than a silence.

THIS CAST IS A DECLINED REACH, DONE PROPERLY. aider_shim charter edge (o) records the same measurement from the consumer's side and explicitly refuses to edit inference_domain's code from another component's voyage (Law 6: the owner alone gates writes). The ticket is what that refusal is supposed to produce.
